protocol: Fresh follow-up set authored after the original frozen evaluation. It tests bounded strategy selection on new wording for one fixed allocation pattern; it is not an executable-workload or GPU-correctness benchmark. Transient transport/capacity failures may be retried up to two times and every attempt is recorded. Wrong, malformed, or unsupported model answers are never retried.

cases.contract: For every query row, return the position of its nearest reference row. If two are equally close, return the smaller position.
The output has shape [N] and contains integer argmin indices along the reference dimension, one for each query.
Map each query to its closest database entry and return that entry's index; distances themselves are not requested.
Produce one integer per query: the number of reference points whose Euclidean distance is less than or equal to 1.0.
For each query, count all references inside the unit-radius neighborhood, including points exactly on its edge.
Return a length-N vector of neighbor totals under the condition distance(q, r) <= radius, where radius is 1.0.
Return the two nearest reference indices for every query, sorted from nearest to second-nearest.
For each query, output the minimum Euclidean distance as a floating-point value; do not output an index.
Keep the full rectangular table: entry [i,j] must be the distance from query i to reference j.
Return one Boolean per query indicating whether any reference is strictly closer than 1.0. The result is a flag, not a count.
Return the nearest reference index only when its distance is below the threshold; otherwise return sentinel -1.
For each query return the list of every reference index inside radius 1.0, rather than the number of such references.
